definition: Maximum mass (~1.44 solar masses) a stable white dwarf can support via electron degeneracy pressure before collapsing.
context: Above 1.44 M☉ triggers a Type Ia supernova or neutron star collapse.

definition: Pulsating variable stars whose intrinsic luminosity correlates tightly with pulsation period, serving as extragalactic distance ladders.
context: Calibrated first by Henrietta Swan Leavitt in the SMC.

definition: Minimum orbital radius within which a celestial body held together solely by self-gravity disintegrates under tidal forces.
context: Explains planetary ring formation inside the inner orbit of Saturn.

definition: Distance at which 1 astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arcsecond (approximately 3.26 light-years).
context: Derived directly from annual stellar parallax geometry.

definition: Stretching of photon wavelengths caused by metric expansion of space while light travels toward the observer.
context: 1 + z = λ_observed / λ_emitted.

definition: Scatter plot relating stellar luminosity (or absolute magnitude) against effective surface temperature (OBAFGKM spectral class).
context: 90% of stars lie along the hydrogen-fusing Main Sequence band.

definition: Thermonuclear detonation of a carbon-oxygen white dwarf accreting mass near the Chandrasekhar limit, producing uniform peak brightness.
context: Used to discover accelerating cosmic expansion in 1998.

definition: Critical radius where escape velocity reaches the speed of light for a non-rotating spherical mass.
context: R_s = 2GM / c² (~3 km per solar mass).

definition: Maximum mass (~2.17 solar masses) a cold, non-rotating neutron star can support via neutron degeneracy pressure and strong nuclear repulsion before collapsing.
context: Analogous to the Chandrasekhar limit for neutron stars; constrained by NICER and GW170817.

definition: Maximum radiative luminosity a star or accreting object can emit before outward photon radiation pressure balances inward gravitational pull.
context: L_Edd ≈ 3.3 × 10⁴ L☉ · (M / M☉) for pure ionized hydrogen.

definition: Blackbody peak emission wavelength is inversely proportional to absolute surface temperature.
context: λ_max · T ≈ 2.898 × 10⁶ nm·K; explains why O-stars glow blue and M-stars glow red.

definition: Total power radiated by a spherical blackbody scales with surface area and the fourth power of effective temperature.
context: L = 4πR²σT⁴; lets astronomers deduce stellar radius from luminosity and spectrum.

definition: Square of an orbit's period is proportional to the cube of its semi-major axis divided by total system mass.
context: P² = 4π²a³ / [G(M₁ + M₂)]; primary tool for weighing binary stars and exoplanets.

definition: Minimum mass an interstellar gas cloud must exceed for self-gravity to overcome internal thermal gas pressure and trigger star formation.
context: Scales as T^(3/2) · ρ^(-1/2); cold, dense molecular cores collapse most readily.

definition: Dominant hydrogen-to-helium nuclear fusion pathway inside stars of roughly 1.3 solar masses or less.
context: Converts 4 protons into ⁴He + 2e⁺ + 2νₑ + ~26.7 MeV; dominates in the Sun's core (~1.5 × 10⁷ K).

definition: Catalytic fusion pathway using carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen nuclei to fuse hydrogen into helium in hotter stellar cores.
context: Scales steeply (~T¹⁶) and overtakes the p-p chain above ~1.3 solar masses.

definition: Linear relation between a distant galaxy's recession velocity and its proper distance in an expanding universe.
context: v = H₀ · d; local and CMB measurements of H₀ sit near 67–73 km/s/Mpc.

definition: Thermal blackbody radiation left over from photon decoupling during recombination, redshifted into microwave wavelengths today.
context: Emitted at z ≈ 1100 (~380,000 years post-Big Bang); observed today at T ≈ 2.725 K.

definition: Deflection of light rays from a background source by the curved spacetime of an intervening massive galaxy or cluster.
context: Reveals dark matter mass distributions and produces arcs, multiple images, and Einstein crosses.

definition: Five equilibrium positions in a rotating two-body gravitational system where a small third body maintains fixed relative geometry.
context: JWST orbits Sun-Earth L2 (~1.5 million km anti-sunward) for stable thermal shielding.

definition: Empirical correlation between a spiral galaxy's intrinsic luminosity and the width of its neutral hydrogen rotation curve.
context: L ∝ v_max⁴; serves as a secondary extragalactic distance indicator across tens of megaparsecs.

definition: Relates time-averaged kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy in a bound, relaxed stellar or galaxy cluster system.
context: 2⟨K⟩ + ⟨U⟩ = 0; Fritz Zwicky applied it to the Coma Cluster to infer dark matter.
